label: adaptive-gemini
note: Illustrative stated starting points; live provider calls, no user Chart writes.

context.intention: I maintain a consistent workout routine.
context.actualStartingPoint: I exercise sporadically. I can use three 30-minute slots each week for bodyweight exercise at home.
context.destinationDescription: I maintain a consistent workout routine.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Exercises sporadically with three available 30-minute home bodyweight slots per week.
assumptions: The user has access to a safe space at home for bodyweight exercises.
The three weekly slots are reliably available.

routeDesign.complexityReason: Building a consistent habit from sporadic exercise requires establishing a reliable weekly anchor, weathering disruption, and sustaining a self-directed rhythm over time.
routeDesign.countReason: Three waypoints map the natural progression from initial routine adherence to resilience and long-term sustainability.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Completing all three scheduled 30-minute home workouts in a single week.

raw.destination: Maintain a consistent workout routine using three weekly 30-minute home sessions.

waypoints.title: Complete first full week of three sessions
waypoints.rationale: Establishes immediate proof of capability within the planned routine.
waypoints.completionCriteria: All three 30-minute home bodyweight sessions completed in one calendar week.

moves.title: Schedule the three 30-minute slots in the calendar
moves.rationale: Secures time for the sessions before the week begins.

moves.title: Select a simple bodyweight exercise sequence
moves.rationale: Reduces decision fatigue during workout time.

moves.title: Complete the first scheduled home session
moves.rationale: Initiates the physical routine.

moves.title: Finish the remaining two sessions of the week
moves.rationale: Secures the first full week of adherence.

waypoints.title: Maintain routine through a disrupted week
waypoints.rationale: Tests adaptability when schedule or energy changes occur.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Three sessions completed during a week with altered routines or low energy.

moves.title: Identify potential schedule conflicts for the upcoming week
moves.rationale: Anticipates disruptions ahead of time.

moves.title: Reschedule any threatened session to an alternative slot
moves.rationale: Preserves the weekly target despite changes.

moves.title: Execute a shortened version if full time is unavailable
moves.rationale: Maintains the habit loop when capacity is low.

moves.title: Review how the disruption was handled
moves.rationale: Reinforces flexibility strategies.

waypoints.title: Sustain self-directed rhythm over a month
waypoints.rationale: Transforms the routine into a stable, autonomous habit.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Three weekly sessions maintained consistently for four consecutive weeks.

moves.title: Track weekly completion without relying on external reminders
moves.rationale: Shifts ownership of the habit inward.

moves.title: Vary exercise movements to sustain physical engagement
moves.rationale: Prevents boredom and plateaus.

moves.title: Assess energy and body changes after four weeks
moves.rationale: Connects routine adherence to tangible physical feedback.

suggestedOneMove.title: Schedule the three 30-minute slots in the calendar
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Secures time for the sessions before the week begins.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus on locking in the three weekly time blocks before worrying about exercise intensity.

context.intention: I successfully complete my first half marathon.
context.actualStartingPoint: I run 5 km comfortably twice a week. I can train three days each week. I have never completed a half marathon.
context.destinationDescription: I successfully complete my first half marathon.

analysis.startingPointSummary: Runs 5 km comfortably twice a week, can train three days a week, no prior half marathon experience.
assumptions: Can dedicate three days per week to running and recovery.
Has running shoes and a safe route for training.

routeDesign.complexityReason: A straightforward endurance progression from a 5 km base to completing a 21.1 km race.
routeDesign.countReason: Three distinct phases cover building the distance base, testing peak endurance, and race completion.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: Extending the long run beyond 5 km while maintaining a comfortable pace across three weekly sessions.

waypoints.title: Establish an extended distance base
waypoints.rationale: Builds cardiovascular capacity and leg strength safely beyond the current 5 km limit.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a single continuous run of 12 km during weekly training.

moves.title: Add one kilometer to the weekly long run
moves.rationale: Gradually increases distance without overloading joints.

moves.title: Maintain two shorter 5 km runs during the week
moves.rationale: Preserves aerobic baseline while building toward the long run.

moves.title: Schedule a rest day immediately following the long run
moves.rationale: Allows muscle tissue repair and energy replenishment.

waypoints.title: Reach peak training distance
waypoints.rationale: Confirms the body can handle near-race distance before tapering.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Complete a single continuous run of 16 km within the three-day training schedule.

moves.title: Incorporate a 14 km long run on the weekend
moves.rationale: Steps up total distance incrementally from the previous phase.

moves.title: Test hydration and fuel strategies during the long run
moves.rationale: Ensures the digestive system tolerates nutrition over longer efforts.

moves.title: Push the long run distance to 16 km
moves.rationale: Provides the necessary physiological stimulus for half marathon readiness.

waypoints.title: Complete the half marathon distance
waypoints.rationale: Executes the final goal of finishing the full 21.1 km event.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Cover the full 21.1 km distance in a single continuous session.

moves.title: Execute a tapered training week with reduced mileage
moves.rationale: Allows muscle glycogen stores to peak and legs to feel fresh.

moves.title: Run the 21.1 km distance at a sustainable pace
moves.rationale: Prevents early burnout and ensures successful completion.

moves.title: Follow the event with hydration and rest
moves.rationale: Supports initial physical recovery after peak exertion.

suggestedOneMove.title: Add one kilometer to the weekly long run
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Starts the progression from your current 5 km baseline.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus on gradual distance increases across your three weekly sessions to build endurance safely.

context.actualStartingPoint: Anchor is launched with 20 paying users. I am the solo developer, with 10 hours a week for growth and no paid advertising budget. I can contact current users and have subscription analytics.

vision.title: A sustainable Anchor business
vision.description: 10,000 paying users who continue using Anchor

analysis.startingPointSummary: Anchor has 20 paying users, solo developer with 10 hours a week for growth, no ad budget, access to current users and subscription analytics.
assumptions: Current users can provide qualitative feedback on retention drivers
Growth must rely on organic or zero-cost acquisition channels given the lack of ad budget
10 hours per week limits the volume of concurrent marketing experiments

routeDesign.complexityReason: Scaling from 20 to 10,000 paying users without a budget requires distinct phases of retention optimization, organic channel validation, and operational scaling.
routeDesign.countReason: Four distinct milestones cover retention stabilization, first tier of organic growth, repeatable acquisition validation, and final scale.

analysis.firstMilestoneEvidence: User interviews conducted and initial retention drop-offs identified from subscription analytics.

waypoints.title: Understand current retention drivers
waypoints.rationale: Before acquiring new users, retaining the existing base ensures growth does not leak.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Completed interviews with at least five current paying users and analyzed subscription analytics to identify primary retention factors.

moves.title: Email 10 current paying users to request a short feedback call
moves.rationale: Direct outreach uncovers why users stay.

moves.title: Review subscription analytics for churn timing
moves.rationale: Identifies exactly when users typically cancel.

moves.title: Synthesize feedback into three core retention drivers
moves.rationale: Isolates what makes the product valuable.

waypoints.title: Reach 100 paying users through direct outreach
waypoints.rationale: Proves early product-market fit beyond the initial cohort.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Active subscriber count reaches 100.

moves.title: List 50 potential users matching current customer profiles
moves.rationale: Builds a targeted outreach list.

moves.title: Send personalized messages offering a direct conversation or trial
moves.rationale: Engages prospects directly without paid ads.

moves.title: Track conversion rate from outreach to subscription
moves.rationale: Measures the effectiveness of direct messaging.

waypoints.title: Establish a repeatable zero-cost acquisition channel
waypoints.rationale: Moving past manual outreach requires a structured channel that generates consistent signups.
waypoints.completionCriteria: A single organic acquisition channel consistently brings in new users each week without paid ads.
requirements: Select one organic channel suited to available skills
Publish content or outreach consistently for four weeks
Measure weekly acquisition numbers from the chosen channel

moves.title: Choose one organic channel such as content, communities, or partnerships
moves.rationale: Focuses limited weekly hours on a single approach.

moves.title: Create a weekly publishing or engagement schedule
moves.rationale: Ensures consistent execution within the 10-hour limit.

moves.title: Review channel performance metrics after two weeks
moves.rationale: Determines if the channel yields sustainable signups.

waypoints.title: Scale to 10,000 paying users
waypoints.rationale: Reaches the ultimate destination by compounding validated acquisition and retention.
waypoints.completionCriteria: Active paid subscriber count reaches 10,000.

moves.title: Optimize onboarding flows to improve conversion efficiency
moves.rationale: Ensures more trial users convert to paid subscriptions.

moves.title: Automate routine customer communication workflows
moves.rationale: Saves developer time as user volume increases.

moves.title: Monitor weekly churn and acquisition rates against target growth curve
moves.rationale: Keeps the business on track toward the final count.

suggestedOneMove.title: Email 10 current paying users to request a short feedback call
suggestedOneMove.rationale: Direct outreach uncovers why users stay and establishes baseline retention insights.

raw.personalizedGuidance: Focus your limited weekly hours on understanding existing retention before scaling outreach.
